behavioral_effects: git-filter-repo --replace-text rewrote 151 commits in a mirror clone, replacing the Logfire token, OpenRouter key, and Google OAuth client secret values in backend/.env.example history with REVOKED; verified by exact-string search over all commits and an unbaselined gitleaks scan (no leaks) before the force-push of main.
.gitleaks-baseline.json is emptied to []; the nightly full-history scan now gates on a genuinely clean history.
compatibility_impact: Every commit SHA from aaec6463 onward changed; the HEAD tree hash is byte-identical pre and post rewrite, so no code changed. Older governance change records and external references naming pre-rewrite SHAs (baseline_commit fields, CI run links) now point at orphaned commits; they remain honest as history but no longer resolve in a fresh clone.
follow_up: After the owner deletes the three Dependabot branches, re-run make secret-scan to confirm, then proceed with the pre-public hardening session (LICENSE, secret scanning, push protection, branch protection, GHCR visibility).
limitations: Three Dependabot branches on origin (PRs 12, 16, 20) still carry pre-rewrite commits; deleting remote branches was blocked by the tool permission layer, so the owner closes those PRs and deletes their branches, after which Dependabot recreates them from rewritten main.
Orphaned pre-rewrite objects on GitHub are only fully purged by contacting GitHub support; accepted since every leaked credential is revoked.
reason: Go-public preparation: commit aaec6463 and seven descendants carry the now-revoked Logfire token, OpenRouter key, and Google OAuth client secret in backend/.env.example; all three are dead at their providers, so a git-filter-repo replace-text rewrite plus force-push removes the strings before the repository is made public, and the 3-fingerprint gitleaks baseline empties accordingly
rollback: Not meaningfully revertible: pre-rewrite refs exist only on GitHub as orphaned objects and in any stale clones. A stale clone force-pushing main would restore the old history; after going public, treat any such push as an incident.
security_impact: Positive: the three revoked credential strings are removed from every commit reachable from main, locally and on the remote after the force-push. Residuals: GitHub keeps pre-rewrite commits fetchable by SHA until its garbage collection or a support-ticket purge, and three Dependabot PR branches on origin still reference pre-rewrite history until deleted (owner action, permission-gated). All three credentials are already dead at their providers, so the residuals expose only revoked strings.
summary: Rewrite git history to remove the three dead credential strings from backend/.env.example and empty the gitleaks baseline

validators_run.evidence_ref: gitleaks v8.30.1 over the rewritten local history reports no leaks with no baseline; the 3-fingerprint baseline is emptied
